# fastf 3.3.0 — nothing fails quietly

Feature work reached a wall at 3.2.0. Every gate was green, there was not one
`TODO` in the tree, and the honest next move was to go looking for what a green
gate cannot see. Four audits over the engine, the app, the command line and the
test suite found about sixty things. This is what came of them.

The theme is **silence**: every place fastf did the wrong thing, or nothing, and
said so nowhere.

## A project could disappear from your library

fastf finds projects by reading the `PROJECT_INFO.md` in each folder. If it
could not read one — a missing field, a stray indent, one character saved in the
wrong encoding — it skipped the folder and said nothing at all. The project was
still on your disk, with its ID and its notes, and `fastf recent` said "No
projects yet". `fastf reindex`, the command whose entire job is to look again,
reported the smaller count as a success.

`docs/projects.md` invites you to edit that file. So:

- **Only `id` and `template` are load-bearing now.** Delete the `created:` line
  and the project is still a project — the date falls back to the folder's own.
  `folder:` and `path:` were never read back at all.
- **A file fastf genuinely cannot read is named, every time**, with the folder
  and the reason. Fix it and the project comes straight back.

The realistic version of this is a shared drive: a Windows editor saving as the
system codepage rather than UTF-8 turns one accented character into bytes fastf
cannot read.

## The app could crash

Open the settings, arrow down to **Bases**, press Enter — on any terminal
between 16 and 23 rows tall, fastf panicked and died. It survived 80×24 by
exactly one row, which is why the window size everybody tests at never showed
it.

The editor slides up when there is no room below it now, and the three shapes of
arithmetic that caused it have names in one place, so the next box that opens
over a row cannot repeat it.

## A delete could delete a different project

The confirmation named the project under the cursor. The action was built again
when you pressed Enter, from whatever was selected *then* — and a background
rescan can move the cursor if the row it named has left the list. The dialogs
carry their target now, and a target that is gone is a refusal rather than a
neighbour.

While it was there: a template you had worked on for ten minutes could be thrown
away with no question, if you quit through the command palette instead of
pressing Esc.

## Guards that were written down and never ran

fastf refuses to walk more than 64 directories deep, because deeper than that
overflows a thread's stack on Windows and takes the process with it. Three of
the five walks that check that limit reset the counter at every level, so the
check could never fire — including the folder-size scan, which was also the one
running on the smallest stack. All three are bounded now, and so is a template's
declared folder structure.

## Everything else

- A journal note written after a heading you had added to `PROJECT_INFO.md` was
  saved, printed back to you, and never seen again.
- The ID counter read an unreadable counter file as zero, quietly dropping the
  one guard that stops an unplugged drive from restarting your numbering.
- `fastf config set recent-limit` wrote a *different* key than the one it and
  `config show` both printed, so setting it by hand in `config.toml` did nothing.
- Pressing Esc at the template picker was a red error and exit 1; pressing Esc
  one prompt later was a polite "cancelled" and exit 0.
- `fastf register --recursive` printed a green tick and exited 0 when every
  single folder had failed.
- An editor that failed to start was reported as having opened the project.
- The first-run banner went to stdout, so `cd "$(fastf path myproject)"` could
  come back with the banner glued to the front of the path.
- A first run interrupted between the two bundled templates left you with one of
  them, permanently.
- Wide characters — Cyrillic, Japanese, anything two columns wide — put the text
  cursor at roughly half the column it belonged in.
- The templates tab's detail pane could not be scrolled at all, so a template
  longer than the pane had its tail out of reach.
- On a legacy Windows console, twelve success messages drew a box instead of a
  tick.
- A confirmation naming six folders was cut short on a narrow window — the one
  dialog that must not hide what it is about.
- `fastf reconcile` now finds and finishes a rename that was interrupted by a
  power cut or a `kill -9`, which used to leave the project under a hidden name
  that nothing listed.

## Nothing to do

No flag, config key or file format changed. Every `config.toml` and
`PROJECT_INFO.md` written by an earlier fastf still works, and `recent_limit`
now works whichever way you spelled it.
